summary: Make the in-chat per-file diff cards (with per-hunk accept/reject) opt-in and off by default, since most users only review a diff once it becomes a PR. Off collapses a turn's changed files to a single "Changed N files" button that expands the real cards for that turn only; the backend keeps computing and emitting file.edited unconditionally. The phone (React Native) and native Android now fold a turn's file rows the same way: one "Changed N files" row with the turn's line totals, collapsed by default, where the turn's first file row was; a tap opens that turn's compact file rows on this device only (screen state, no stored setting and nothing read from the desktop's chat.showFileDiffs). A turn is everything between two user rows, since neither phone feed carries a turn id.

sharedBackendApi.reason: Render-only change on the desktop client. The git-checkpoint diff computation and the file.edited event (src/main/git/checkpoint.ts, src/shared/provider-events.ts) are unconditional and untouched - every provider still emits one event per changed file per turn regardless of this setting, so mobile/Android and any future consumer keep receiving the same wire data they always did.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change and no migration. The preference is one new row, chat.showFileDiffs, in the existing generic key-value settings table (src/main/db/database.ts). An absent key already means 'no preference' and the reader (hydrateSidebarCollapse in layout-store.ts) treats anything other than the literal string 'true' as off, so an older database (no row) and a newer database (row present) both resolve correctly with no backfill, and an older client that has never heard of the key simply never reads or writes it.

updateRelease.reason: Presentation change only. No package identity, signing, deep-link scheme, update channel, or wire-protocol change; the file.edited IPC/event contract is untouched. The phone's part is JavaScript only, so it can ride the mobile-ota.yml lane (the fingerprint runtimeVersion is unchanged); native Android's ships with its next APK.

automated: npm run typecheck passed for both the main and renderer projects.

npm test passed the full vitest suite including two new tests: layout-store's 'file diff cards opt-in' describe block (default-off, setShowFileDiffCards toggles the flag) and message-list's changedFilesLabel formatting test ('Changed 1 file' / 'Changed 8 files').

npx vitest run tests/unit/mobile-file-groups.test.ts: each turn folds behind one collapsed row where its first file was, only the tapped turn expands, a feed without edits is unchanged, the label counts
npm test --prefix apps/mobile: FileGroupItem renders the count, the totals and its expanded state, and a tap toggles its own turn

cd apps/android && ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest: ThreadFileGroupsTest (the same three rules as the phone); ThreadScreenRegressionTest's file-edit case now expands the group first (instrumented, compiled only)
hardware: Desktop manual verification on this Mac: built with npm run build:fast, launched the app via videos/capture-tour.mjs's own scripted demo fixture (SB_DEMO_ADAPTER=1) with the seeded settings row set to 'false', ran the 'diff-review' scene (a real turn that edits a file) and confirmed the turn collapses to a 'Changed 1 file' button with no per-hunk controls visible. Re-seeded the row to 'true' and reran the same scene, confirming the cards render exactly as before (header + Keep all/Reject all + hunks), matching the pre-existing tour clip. Separately launched a fresh Electron instance with an isolated --user-data-dir and screenshotted Settings > General > Responses, confirming the new 'Show file diff cards in chat' checkbox renders unchecked by default with its description.

No live remote-backend (WsHost/SSH-tunnelled) session was used to confirm the setting behaves the same when a session is served over the wire instead of the local Electron IPC host - the setting is read through the same window.api.settings surface either way, so no divergence is expected, but it was not exercised.
Neither phone's Changed N files row was tapped on a device or emulator (none was available); the instrumented ThreadScreenRegressionTest was compiled, not run.
